## EBS Hub mission

The Hub is platform for connecting the department's research, education, open-source software and external partnerships to maximise real-world impact.

::: {.mission-question}
<p><strong>Question:</strong> What are the blockers for your work to connect through these themes?</p>
:::

## The Hub can only connect what it can find {.statement-slide .full-width-statement}

<p class="statement">A clear profile helps the right people recognise your work, understand where it applies and start a useful conversation.</p>

::: {.fragment}
It also helps me to work out what opportunities are useful for who, saving both of us (mainly you) time.
:::


::: {.notes}
Keep this short. The practical point is discoverability. Avoid framing profile maintenance as compliance or performance assessment.
:::

## A useful profile answers four questions

<ol class="four-questions">
  <li><span>01</span><strong>What problems do you work on?</strong></li>
  <li><span>02</span><strong>What methods, software or data do you bring?</strong></li>
  <li><span>03</span><strong>Where has the work been used?</strong></li>
  <li><span>04</span><strong>What kinds of conversations are welcome?</strong></li>
</ol>

::: {.notes}
Ask participants to use these questions as an editing test. They do not need polished marketing copy; they need a truthful, current account in plain language.
:::

## Updating your Monash profile in Pure {.pure-guide-slide}

<ol class="pure-steps">
  <li><span>01</span><div><strong>Open myResearch</strong><small>Sign in and open Pure, the project, output and profile system.</small></div></li>
  <li><span>02</span><div><strong>Choose Edit profile</strong><small>Start from your personal overview. Open the editor for your public profile.</small></div></li>
  <li><span>03</span><div><strong>Update the useful fields</strong><small>Prioritise your biography, research interests, keywords and links.</small></div></li>
  <li><span>04</span><div><strong>Preview, then save</strong><small>Check what the public page will show. Research outputs are managed through their own records.</small></div></li>
</ol>

<p class="pure-guide-links"><a href="https://www.monash.edu/myResearch/home">Open myResearch</a> · <a href="https://www.monash.edu/library/researchers/researcher-profiles">Profile and author ID guide</a> · <a href="profile-prompt.html">Open the Gemini prompt</a> · <a href="downloads/researcher-profile-drafter.zip" download>Download the agent skill</a></p>

::: {.notes}
Demonstrate these four actions live before starting the ten-minute editing block. Pure populates the public Monash researcher profile. The myResearch home page includes the current “Updating your Public Profile” quick guide and a separate guide for claiming research outputs.

Sources: https://www.monash.edu/myResearch/home and https://www.monash.edu/library/researchers/researcher-profiles (accessed 12 November 2026).
:::

## 2 · Monash profile, ORCID & Scholar <span class="time-chip">15 minutes</span> {.work-slide}

<div class="panel-title">Highest-value edits</div>

- first two sentences of the biography
- research keywords people would actually search
- current projects and external applications
- software, data, training or consulting links

::: {.three-column-work}

::: {.work-instruction}
<div class="panel-title">Open Pure</div>

[Monash myResearch](https://www.monash.edu/myResearch/home)

Use **Pure → Edit profile**. Preview the public version before saving.

[Monash profile and author ID guide](https://www.monash.edu/library/researchers/researcher-profiles)
:::

::: {.work-instruction}
<div class="panel-title">ORCID</div>

- check employment and preferred name
- add missing works by DOI or import tool
- make useful items publicly visible

[Open your ORCID record](https://orcid.org/my-orcid)
:::

::: {.work-instruction}
<div class="panel-title">Google Scholar</div>

- remove work that is not yours
- merge duplicates
- add missing articles
- check homepage and affiliation

[Open Google Scholar](https://scholar.google.com/citations)
:::
:::

::: {.notes}
Tell participants to prioritise the top of the biography and keywords. Offer help locating Pure. If they lack access, have them draft the exact replacement text so the time still produces something useful.
:::

## If you finish early

::: {.early-list}
- Add a link to useful software, data, a project page or training material.
- Replace a broad keyword with language an external partner might search.
- Check that ORCID and Scholar link back to a current homepage.
- Note anything the corpus still misses after your edits.
:::

<p class="caveat">Public profiles and the Hub corpus will not update at the same speed.</p>

::: {.notes}
Use this slide while circulating. Remind participants that source refreshes and public indexing can lag behind their edits.
:::

## A better starting point for the Hub {.closing-slide}

<p class="statement">Current profiles help The Hub bring you better-matched conversations.</p>

<div class="closing-actions">
<span>Save your edits</span>
<span>Record unresolved corrections</span>
<span>Tell us what you want the Hub to notice</span>
</div>

::: {.notes}
Close by asking people to save, note unresolved access issues and tell the Hub about priorities that no public profile can infer. Reinforce that the goal is better support for their work.
:::
